commit.message:
Fix: store epoch on globalThis to prevent separate module instances from diverging (#396)

* Fix: store epoch on globalThis to prevent separate module instances from diverging

Fixes #371

When nanostores is bundled separately in different parts of an application
(e.g., tree-shaking separates core from React), each bundle can end up with
its own epoch instance. This causes computed stores to not receive updates
from atom stores in different bundles, because the epoch counters are not
shared.

The fix stores epoch on globalThis.nanostores to ensure all module instances
share the same counter, regardless of how they are bundled.

* Use nanostoresEpoch as global key per review feedback

* Address review comments: fix comment and update size limits

- Update comment to reference globalThis.nanostoresEpoch instead of globalThis.nanostores
- Update Atom size limit: 271 B → 311 B
- Update Popular Set size limit: 802 B → 835 B

* Fix: export shared NANOSTORES_EPOCH object instead of primitive epoch value

The original implementation had a bug: 'export let epoch = NANOSTORES.epoch' captured
the initial value (0) as a local variable, and 'epoch++' in notify() incremented the
local copy, not the shared global. This meant separate module instances still had
diverging epoch counters.

Fix: Export the shared object 'NANOSTORES_EPOCH' and use NANOSTORES.epoch++ for
increments, ensuring all module instances share the same epoch counter.

Changes per review feedback from ai:
- atom/index.js: Export NANOSTORES_EPOCH (the shared global object) instead of epoch
- atom/index.js: Use NANOSTORES.epoch++ instead of epoch++
- computed/index.js: Import and use NANOSTORES_EPOCH.epoch instead of epoch
- package.json: Update Popular Set size limit from 835 B to 845 B

* Use ||= for cleaner initialization, per gismya's suggestion

Saving 11 B on Atom (300 B vs 307 B) and 8 B on Popular Set (837 B vs 845 B).
